Maria (PM): quick sync — we need a concise mapping of roadmap scenarios for the Efficiency Adviser (batching / caching / quant recommendations + eval-alerts). proposing 3 launch scenarios: 'Low-friction', 'Ops-first', 'Enterprise-bake'. thoughts?
Derek (Eng): +1. would like to see tradeoffs per scenario (latency p50/p95, predicted token-cost delta, operational burnout).
Sasha (ML): also include expected model-concordance risk (how often recomendations change outputs). for quant recs we should attach guardrails: e.g., warn if quality delta > 2% on eval set.
Leo (Solutions): customers will ask for a quick ROI calc. can we make a tiny matrix: "impact buckets" (cost-save / latency-risk / integration-effort) so SEs can demo fast?
Maria (PM): yes — here's a draft 3x3 mapping I'm thinking. Paste: 

Scenario: Low-friction
- Target: self-serve customers, minimal config
- Features: read-only recommendations, opt-in batch suggestions, inline UI tips
- Acceptance criteria: <1 extra API call per request, rollout via feature-flag, no SLA changes
- Expected benefits: ~10-15% token cost reduction (heuristic batching + prefix cache)
- Risks: limited quality tuning, some customers may need more control

Scenario: Ops-first
- Target: platform/ops teams with moderate config needs
- Features: orchestrated batching presets, KV-prefix caching policies, quantization suggestion engine (safe presets), eval-triggered alerts to Sentry/console
- Acceptance criteria: documented SLO tradeoffs, can throttle recommendations, observable regressions via eval hook
- Expected benefits: ~20-35% cost reduction on batchy workloads, slightly higher p95 latency due to batching windows
- Risks: need autoscaling tweaks, initial ops integration work

Scenario: Enterprise-bake
- Target: Dedicated/Private deployments requiring strict controls
- Features: full rollout API, canary-by-tenant, automatic quant suggestion with diff reports, eval-triggered automated hold/backout flow, config-as-code
- Acceptance criteria: KMS/HSM compatibility for private, audit logs for every recommendation decision, SLI thresholds for auto-backout
- Expected benefits: 25-50% cost reduction for high-volume flows, preserve enterprise SLAs
- Risks: heavier engineering + compliance work, longer sales cycles

Derek (Eng): nice. for the Ops-first scenario we should add a small example of batching policy DSL so engs can estimate complexity. e.g.:
```
batch_policy:
  name: user-session-window
  max_delay_ms: 50
  max_tokens: 2048
  prefer_low_latency: false
```
Sasha (ML): and for quant recs include a simple eval snippet that we can run nightly: 
```
# run on validation set
apply_quant(candidate) -> generate_outputs
compute_concordance(orig_outputs, quant_outputs) -> percent_diff
if percent_diff > 2%: flag_for_manual_review
```
Leo (Solutions): on ROI matrix — suggest we provide a small calc sheet for SEs: inputs = avg tokens/session, sessions/day, current cost/token, expected % reduction. returns monthly $ saved. can we automate a one-click estimator in console later?
Jamie (ProdDev): yes on the estimator. short-term: add a simple CSV template. long-term: embed estimator + sample dataset upload in console.
Maria (PM): prioritization ask: we can only pick 2 initial deliverables for Q3 slice. proposed priority: 1) Low-friction (fast win), 2) Ops-first (highest impact for mid-market). Enterprise-bake as Q4. anyone disagree?
Derek (Eng): agree but push some platform work early (prefix cache primitives + safe quant paths) — those land across all scenarios. label them as infra dependencies in the ticket.
Sasha (ML): agree. also we need an eval-trigger event taxonomy: sample-level alerts (data drift), model-level alerts (concordance drop), infra-level (batch latency spikes). tie them to severity levels.
Leo (Solutions): customers will want control over alert noise. recommend default thresholds conservative (low false positive), and provide advanced controls.
Maria (PM): action items: 
- Maria: refine ROI matrix + CSV template (due EOD Fri)
- Derek: prototype prefix-cache primitive + batch_policy proto (PR by next Tue)
- Sasha: write eval snippet + taxonomy doc draft (sync Wed)
- Leo: build SE ROI one-pager + sample scripts (demo Wed)
- Jamie: add acceptance criteria to JIRA tickets (include checklist for KMS/audit/SLIs)
ops-bot: note created: OPT-423 Efficiency Adviser roadmap mapping (assignee: Maria) :spiral_calendar:
Maria (PM): thanks — if no objections I'll lock the Q3 slice on Friday and start allocating eng points. please poke in-thread if you see conflicts. :thumbsup:
Derek (Eng): will raise any infra blockers before EOD Thu.
Sasha (ML): adding a short eval harness tomorrow.
Leo (Solutions): prepping two customer excerpts to validate ROI assumptions (AcmeHealth, Shoply).
Jamie (ProdDev): will add the acceptance checklist to the story and tag security for Enterprise-bake.
Maria (PM): great. closing loop unless anything else. small ask: keep the launch messaging simple — "Efficiency Adviser helps reduce token cost with safe, explainable recommendations".
Leo (Solutions): sounds good. :rocket:
